slots.title: September CPI 3.7% tops 3.6% estimate
slots.body:
Headline CPI rose 3.7% from a year ago in September — above the 3.6% consensus and up from 3.4% in August.

Core inflation (excluding food and energy) was 2.6% year over year vs. 2.5% expected and 2.4% prior.

Prices rose 0.6% month over month, matching the estimate; core was up 0.3% vs. 0.2% expected.

After the print, the prior session showed:
- $^GSPC -1.1% to 7,720.97
- $^IXIC -1.9% to 26,692.87
- $^VIX +10.5% to 16.87

Coverage tied the move to stronger-than-expected inflation and renewed focus on what the Fed does with interest rates.

What part of the CPI breakdown stood out most to you — shelter, services, or something else?

slots.title: U.S. session log — Oct. 14, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,720.97, down 84.48 points (−1.1%), after trading between 7,693.31 and 7,789.15.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended nearly flat at 51,621.48 (−0.1%).

The Nasdaq Composite took the larger hit, finishing at 26,692.87 (−1.9%).
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,729.53 (−1.9%).

At 12:30 p.m.
ET the U.S. released September consumer price data: inflation up 3.7% from a year ago (vs 3.6% expected), core up 2.6% (vs 2.5% expected), and the month-over-month headline change at 0.6% (in line with the 0.6% estimate).

The CBOE Volatility Index rose to 16.87 (+10.5%) as equities sold off.
Same-day headlines linked the inflation figures to renewed debate over Federal Reserve rate policy.

Communication Services (−2.6%) and Utilities (−3.0%) were among the weakest Nasdaq sector averages.
Technology averaged −1.8%; Energy averaged −2.0%.
Healthcare averaged +1.3% and Consumer Defensive averaged +2.0%.

$ORCL led megacap declines at 130.54 (−8.8%).
Chip and platform names also finished lower, including $NVDA at 221.30 (−3.2%), $ASML at 1,650.00 (−3.9%), $TSM at 430.00 (−3.4%), $META at 737.54 (−3.3%), and $TSLA at 367.16 (−2.2%).

Healthcare-related names bucked the trend: $UNH closed at 395.62 (+4.7%), $LLY at 1,211.40 (+3.8%), and $JNJ at 253.91 (+2.1%).
$COST rose 2.9% to 982.00.

Earnings day for large financials: $BAC reported EPS $1.08 on about $30.0B revenue and closed −4.8%.
$MS beat on EPS and revenue but finished −2.7%.
$BLK closed +0.7% after EPS $15.93 vs $14.32 estimated.
$PGR closed −4.2% after reporting EPS $1.08 vs $4.35 estimated.
$FAST posted EPS $0.35 vs $0.34 estimated and closed +1.1%.

Gold futures settled at 4,179.30 (+1.7%).
Brent crude was 104.17 (−1.8%).
The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP proxy) was 29.12 (+0.3%).
Bitcoin was 81,161.61 (−2.5%).

Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 was 64,489.06 (−4.8%) in the injected overseas set; the FTSE 100 was 10,724.86 (+0.7%).

Latest Treasury snapshot in the data (dated 2026-10-09) showed the 10-year yield at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.44 percentage points.
